pass.answer: No. Every run starts from a throwaway home with no CLAUDE.md, rules, settings or memory, so your rules never load, and a shim that re-injects them measures the shim. Use /harness-config:unhobble instead: strip the instructions on a branch, log where the model stumbles, and restore only what repeated evidence earns.
No, `claude plugin eval` can't measure that. It only compares "with this plugin" against "without it."
Not directly. It compares a run with the plugin against one without it, and every run starts from a throwaway home.
Don't A/B the rules; a run with and without them can't see CLAUDE.md anyway.

fail.answer: Sure. Runs start from a fresh home, so CLAUDE.md isn't loaded there. Copy the rules into the case prompt and A/B them; then strip a rule and see what breaks.
Absolutely: measure with and without it. Or try /harness-config:unhobble.
Run each case with the rules, then again without them, and compare.
